title: In Situ and Operando X-ray Microscopy for Aqueous Batteries
content: Aqueous batteries with water-based electrolyte offer a safer, inexpensive alternative to Li-ion battery technology, which is particularly important for large, grid-based energy storage [1,2]. Today’s commercial Li-ion batteries use expensive, flammable electrolytes with cathode materials that can release oxygen at high temperatures or at high operating voltages [3,4]. Recent fires at Li-ion battery energy storage plants highlight the need for large-scale, fire-proof energy storage solutions [5,6].
